newsitem.title: INDIA: India to create fresh 500,000-tonne sugar buffer.
newsitem.headline: India to create fresh 500,000-tonne sugar buffer.

text.p: The Indian government has decided to create an additional 500,000-tonne sugar buffer stock for one year, the Food Ministry said on Friday.
The ministry said in a statement that an existing 500,000-tonne sugar buffer would be extended for another year.
The statement said the cost of the buffer would be met from the Sugar Development Fund (SDF).
The government took the decision due to good sugar output in the 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) season and to help sugar mills to liquidate their cane payment arrears, it said.
India produced a record 16.4 million tonnes of sugar in the 1995/96 season. As of October 1, it had nearly 8.0 million tonnes of sugar in stock compared to 5.4 million one year earlier.
The sugar industry had asked the government to add 1.5 million tonnes to the existing sugar buffer of 500,000 tonnes.
Industry officials say a government buffer stock spares mill owners the expense of holding inventory, providing them with funds to clear accounts with sugarcane farmers.
